summary: APM feed s075_single is degraded: 17.1% of TCP sessions (18/105) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. APM requires bidirectional traffic and will see incomplete transactions. All other checks (duplicates, drops, overload, VLAN, encryption) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Bidirectional aggregation failure: only one direction of TCP sessions is reaching the APM port. Most likely asymmetric routing with separate TAP/SPAN inputs not aggregated, or packet broker forwarding each direction to different tool ports without flow-aware aggregation. 18 of 105 sessions affected (17.1%).
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to correlate request/response for latency, transaction completion and dependency mapping. One-way flows appear as incomplete transactions, causing inaccurate response-time calculations, false errors, and missed application performance traces.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same APM tool port using bidirectional 5-tuple hashing so the APM sees complete request/response pairs and can correctly measure performance.
